title: Western Xia
capsule: The Tangut state that became Western Xia had its roots in 982, when Li Jiqian broke from Song allegiance in the Ordos region and began building an autonomous base; his son Li Deming (r. 1004-1032) consolidated Tangut power and extended it westward. In 1038 Li Deming's son Li Yuanhao (Emperor Jingzong) formally declared the Tangut empire, adopting imperial ritual, a native Tangut script, and the capital Xingqing (Yinchuan), and fought Song and Liao to a negotiated peace in 1044. Ten emperors in all ruled Western Xia as a major regional power contesting the Song, Liao, and Jin, until Genghis Khan's Mongols besieged and annihilated the state in 1227.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory along the Hexi Corridor is well-defined by Chinese dynastic cartography and administrative records; nomadic steppe boundaries to the north and northwest are approximate and inferred from military campaign accounts.
